args.message: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/banker-rounding-fin-212
args.title: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) in round_money per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build of payments-service was failing because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

This PR changes `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, as specified in FIN-212 and in the function's docstring.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP` -> `rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN`

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986`: passed.
- `test_half_even` checks 2.675 -> 2.68 and 2.665 -> 2.66.

Note: this changes rounding for exact-half values (e.g. 2.665 now rounds to 2.66 rather than 2.67). Please check that this matches finance expectations for FIN-212.

trace.final:
The nightly failure is fixed and the pull request is open for review from alex: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

- **Cause:** `round_money` in `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but its docstring and FIN-212 call for banker's rounding.
- **Change:** On branch `fix/banker-rounding-fin-212`, I switched the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. That is the only code change.
- **CI:** Run `ci-0001` passed on commit `08d3cd5986`.
- **PR:** I opened it against `main` with alex as the reviewer. I did not merge it. Merging into main needs a code owner's approval under policy.

The PR description notes one behavior change: exact-half values now round to the even neighbor, so 2.665 becomes 2.66 instead of 2.67. Alex should confirm this matches what finance expects under FIN-212.

content.text: I'll start by reading the failing test and the source file.

The code uses `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but the docstring and FIN-212 call for `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. The test expectations match half-even: 2.675 → 2.68 (7 is odd, so it rounds up to the even 8) and 2.665 → 2.66 (6 is already even). I'll create a branch and make that change.
